The market is not just reacting to the fact pattern itself; it is deciding whether the story deserves a better multiple, a higher confidence level, or a narrower margin for disappointment.

sections.heading: What the market may be pricing in right or wrong
sections.body: Watch whether the story improves access to capital or makes funding harder for weaker peers. Sometimes the market is right to move quickly because the new fact changes the range of possible outcomes. Sometimes it over-credits a headline before checking whether the economics are durable, repeatable, and profitable.

sections.heading: Relevant comparison
sections.body: A useful parallel is Earlier capex cycles where demand moved from the obvious winners into suppliers and infrastructure. In that earlier setup, companies with backlog, margin, and durable customers earned more lasting credit than commodity suppliers. What rhymes is the current story shows demand spreading across the value chain. What is different this time is revenue growth alone does not prove margin quality or durable economics. The bottom line is use the precedent to test whether demand turns into profit and cash flow.
